description: seed baseline unmodified: per-turbine GRU x134 official recipe
re-anchor tail on metric-optimal constant from scored-eligible train records (+66kW); worse on all five folds
add farm diurnal cycle (1 harmonic zero-mean) ramped over long horizon; worse on 4 of 5 folds
uniform -66.5kW tail shift ramped over 24h; mean -0.12 but better on only 2 of 5 folds and nearly all of the gain is F5 (-1.84) - inside noise treat as unestablished
refit all 5 folds with hidden=128 (relaxed 40/8/0.9 schedule) into .cache/ckpt_005/{fold}/; 134 ckpts per fold, 3h29m wall clock
hidden=128 retrained ckpt_005; mean -0.10 vs parent but better on only 3 of 5 folds - inside noise; 18x slower to score
per-column Scaler (was single global scalar; Wspd arrived at 0.016 sd, Pab at 0.002) hidden=128 into .cache/ckpt_007/{fold}/
per-column normalization ckpt_007; worse on all five folds
remove the -66.5kW tail shift; mean +0.06 so shift retained, but no-shift is BETTER on 3 of 5 folds and loses only via F5 (+1.91) - reinforces that 004 is an F5 artefact
metric loss 0.5*(RMSE+MAE) replaces MSE hidden=128 into .cache/ckpt_010/{fold}/; targets the graded objective not the conditional mean
metric loss ckpt_010; much worse on F1-F4 (+0.6 to +3.3) and better only on F5 (-1.59); same signature as the 004 tail shift so both are F5 artefacts of predicting lower
ensemble ckpt_005+ckpt_007 averaging kW forecasts; worse on all five folds - the two models errors are too correlated for averaging to buy anything

replace 134-GRU baseline with fitted linear shrinkage (172 lines no checkpoints no training); mean +0.03 vs parent ie a tie 30x inside noise but better on 3 of 5 folds and lower fold_std - KEPT ON THE SIMPLICITY CRITERION not on score
add 24h power level and 1h wind speed as predictors; worse mainly via F4 (+1.37) - with 1.8M rows this is non-stationarity of the fitted relation not overfitting
add only 1h wind speed as second predictor; +0.015 ie a tie so wind speed adds nothing beyond current power - second independent confirmation after the GRU per-column test
add farm-mean power as cross-sectional predictor (separates faulted from becalmed); better on 4 of 5 folds but F1 +0.39 drags the mean - a tie
fit beta on most recent half of training (persistence measured non-stationary, later halves stronger in 4 of 5 folds); +0.05 ie a tie, lowest fold_std so far 3.94

50/50 ensemble of GRU (ckpt_005) and linear shrinkage; beats BOTH parents - better than GRU on 4 of 5 folds and than linear on 3 of 5 - genuine cross-class decorrelation unlike the two-GRU ensemble in 012

gradient-boosted third model class (xgboost on history state + horizon); 6.6MW worse - only ~9400 effectively independent origins behind 2.7M correlated rows and trees cannot express the smooth horizon decay
swap ensemble linear member for the farm-predictor variant; +0.014 ie identical, better on 4 of 5 folds but F1 drags - simpler member retained
drop the -66.5kW tail shift from the ensemble GRU member; +0.19 so shift retained - better on 3 of 5 folds again and loses via F5 (+1.07)
per-turbine beta instead of pooled (component test for a 3rd ensemble member); identical to pooled (-0.0006) because beta spread across turbines is only 0.033 vs mean 0.292 - no diversity to add
nonparametric binned response curve replacing the linear beta; +0.23 worse despite the nonlinearity being real in-sample - fifth confirmation that added flexibility does not transfer
level window k=1 (chosen on training data where it beat k=6 on every fold); +0.06 ie a tie - the training-data-optimal window did not transfer either

add blade pitch to the ensemble linear member (separates feathered/shut-down from becalmed); -0.028 better on 3 of 5 folds - inside noise but the same framework with the farm predictor scored 43.738 so pitch itself is worth ~0.04

add power-curve residual (power minus what the fitted farm power curve says the wind should give); -0.066 and better on 4 of 5 folds - raw wind speed alone was useless, the interaction with power is what identifies curtailment
add a 24h residual window alongside the 1h one; +0.004 ie identical, better on 3 of 5 - sustained-fault signal adds nothing over the transient one
add farm-wide power-curve residual (grid curtailment signal); -0.002 ie indistinguishable from zero for an extra predictor - DISCARDED ON THE SIMPLICITY CRITERION not on score

add the seed h=48 GRU as a second GRU member at quarter weight (cheap proxy for whether a 2nd-seed retrain would help the ensemble); +0.034 worse - second confirmation after 012 that within-class GRU averaging does not pay
per-turbine power curve so wake losses stop being booked as curtailment; -0.006 ie 0.014% for ~15 lines - DISCARDED ON THE SIMPLICITY CRITERION consistent with 028
add yaw misalignment |Wdir| as a leading underperformance signal; +0.021 worse - the residual already carries the consequence and the cause adds nothing
shrink beta 0.89 toward climatology per its measured 35% cross-period instability; worse on ALL FIVE folds - the fitted beta is not too large
inflate beta by 1.11 (mirror of the 0.89 shrink that failed); BETTER ON ALL FIVE FOLDS -0.076 - validation blocks follow their training window and later periods are measurably more persistent
beta scale 1.21 (pooled curve rescaled onto the recent half); BETTER ON ALL FIVE FOLDS again -0.059 - optimum lies above 1.21
beta scale 1.50; -0.113 better on 4 of 5 folds (F3 +0.03) - optimum still higher
beta scale 1.87 (full trend extrapolation); -0.014 only and now better on just 2 of 5 folds - at the flat top of the curve
cap inflated beta at 1.0 (cannot be more persistent than persistence); -0.081 better on 4 of 5 - protects the short horizon where scale 1.87 was overshooting to 1.75
beta scale 2.50 under the cap; +0.004 flat - F1/F2 keep improving (-0.37 -0.32) while F3/F4/F5 worsen, so the scale is now trading folds and 1.87 is the optimum
modulate beta scale per window by persistence measured in that infile 14-day history; +0.39 worse on 4 of 5 - recent observed persistence does not predict persistence over the horizon

amplify GRU deviation from its flat anchor by 1.87 bounded by full persistence (same mean-vs-median correction as the linear beta); -0.026 but better on only 2 of 5 folds - SCEPTICAL, F1/F2 gain ~0.3 while F3/F4/F5 all lose
gentler GRU amplification 1.40; -0.004 vs 1.87 ie tied in mean but a better balanced fold profile (3 of 5 better vs 037 rather than 2) - knob is flat between 1.4 and 1.9

drop the tail shift now amplification is in place; +0.157 so shift retained - better on 3 of 5 and loses via F5 (+1.05) again, and fold_std drops to 3.90 without it which confirms it is an F5-specific correction
amplify the averaged ensemble output about climatology to restore spread lost to averaging; -0.0007 ie pure noise and again only 2 of 5 folds - DISCARDED ON THE SIMPLICITY CRITERION
per-turbine power curve retested in the corrected program (wake losses no longer booked as curtailment); -0.013 better on 3 of 5 - was only -0.006 before amplification
farm-wide residual retested in the corrected program; -0.0004 ie noise - DISCARDED ON THE SIMPLICITY CRITERION
fit the beta multiplier per horizon against 0.5(RMSE+MAE) on training rows instead of the fixed 1.87+cap; +0.174 worse and 4x slower - the training-period-optimal multiplier does not transfer

drop the GRU member entirely; +0.42 so the GRU earns its keep - but note the linear model ALONE now beats the seed GRU baseline (44.207) by 0.54 with no networks and the lowest fold_std of the run (3.44)
GRU member alone for the record; 43.796 vs linear-alone 43.665 vs ensemble 43.245 - members within 0.13 of each other so 50/50 stays principled, and the ensemble beats both by 0.42-0.55
cap only the persistence coefficient rather than all of them elementwise; +0.006 neutral - the pitch and residual coefficients were never actually being clamped

fit the linear member in cube-root power space to reach the conditional median via a monotone transform; +1.66 worse - the back-transform lowers predictions systematically so F5 gains 2.5 and every other fold loses 1-3, same signature as 011
fit coefficients on the recent half of training combined with the 1.87 inflation; -0.009 and better on 4 of 5 folds - the two compound rather than double-count
add internal-minus-ambient temperature as a slow running-state signal; +0.002 neutral - adds nothing over the power-curve residual
beta scale 1.60 expecting the recent-half fit to have already supplied part of the inflation; +0.038 worse so 1.87 stands - expectation wrong, the two are not substitutes
drop blade pitch as a simplification check; +0.097 worse so it stays - contributes more now (0.097) than when first added (0.028)

bound the persistence coefficient to [0,1]; -0.031 - the raw 48h beta is ~-0.003 ie no signal, and inflating it by 1.87 was asserting -0.09 anti-persistence across the part of the horizon that dominates the score

inflate only the persistence row leaving pitch and residual at their OLS values; +0.097 worse - the state coefficients benefit from inflation too so the mean-vs-median attenuation is broader than persistence alone
isotonic non-increasing persistence curve; rejected with runtime error - the import patch anchor did not match so IsotonicRegression was undefined
isotonic non-increasing persistence curve (import fixed); -0.004 ie noise, only F1 moved - the curve is already near-monotone after the [0,1] bound, not worth a sklearn dependency
nearest-5-neighbour mean power as a spatial denoiser (first use of the turbine location file); +0.040 worse - the local average adds noise rather than removing it
add idle fraction (share of the last hour with Patv<=0) as a state predictor; -0.013 better on 3 of 5 with two unchanged - one physical split point works where 24 nonparametric bins lost 0.23
add reactive power Prtv as a grid-state predictor; +0.183 worse
add a 24h idle fraction alongside the 1h one (sustained downtime vs a momentary lull); -0.041 better on 4 of 5 folds
add a 3-day idle fraction on top of 1h and 24h; +0.083 worse - the sustained-downtime timescale has an optimum at 24h
add 24h blade pitch for sustained feathering alongside the 24h idle fraction; +0.019 worse - redundant with idle
drop the tail shift from the final program; +0.159 so it stays - FOURTH time (021 042 065) removal is better on 3 of 5 folds and loses only via F5 (+1.02), fold_std falls to 3.97 without it
tilt ensemble weight to 0.6 linear / 0.4 GRU on measured member quality; -0.003 ie noise - 50/50 kept as simpler and equally good
exponential age weighting (half-life 0.5 window) replacing the hard recent-half cut; +0.074 worse - the cut is more aggressive (oldest rows get 0 not 25%) so stronger recency is what helps

shorter age half-life 0.25; +0.150 worse than the hard cut and worse than half-life 0.5 - the cut wins for some other reason than aggressiveness, likely that it recentres predictors on the recent window too
drop blade pitch now that idle fractions exist (redundancy check); +0.053 worse - pitch and idle carry different information, both stay
retest a 24h residual window alongside the idle fractions; +0.071 worse - idle already carries the sustained-state information
re-probe GRU amplification at 1.70; -0.003 ie below the ~0.01 noise threshold applied throughout - not adopted, keeping the value would be fitting the knob to these 75 windows
per-column GRU (ckpt_007) as the ensemble member; rejected - that checkpoint set stores per-column scalers and this code path lost the target-stats helper when 008 was reverted
per-column GRU (ckpt_007) as the ensemble member, scaler handling fixed; +0.315 worse than ckpt_005
ABLATION no beta inflation (BETA_SHRINK=1.0); isolates the single largest gain of the run
ABLATION persistence coefficient not floored at zero (upper bound only)
ABLATION coefficients fitted on the full training window instead of the recent half
ABLATION pooled power curve instead of per-turbine (wake losses booked as curtailment again)
ABLATION no GRU anchor amplification (GRU_AMPLIFY=1.0)
ABLATION no power-curve residual predictor; rejected - dropping Resid also dropped Wspd from the columns read while the power curve still needs it (ablation artefact not a finding)
ABLATION no idle-fraction predictors (1h and 24h)
ABLATION linear member alone, no GRU
ABLATION GRU member alone, no linear model
ABLATION no power-curve residual predictor (Wspd kept available for the curve)
drop the recent-half fit and per-turbine curve together (ablation showed +0.010 and +0.004); +0.020 for -27 lines - a defensible simplicity trade but the mechanical rule keeps the better score
fourth retrain: same config as ckpt_005 but base seed 1234 into .cache/ckpt_085/{fold}/; controlled test of within-class ensembling since 012 and 029 both averaged a WEAKER second GRU
SENSITIVITY beta scale 1.30 on the final program (mapping the response surface of the run's biggest lever)
SENSITIVITY beta scale 1.60 on the final program
beta scale 2.10; -0.018 vs 1.87 and the response surface over 1.0/1.3/1.6/1.87/2.1/2.4 is smooth to a flat optimum here - but better on only 2 of 5 folds so treat the last 0.018 as unestablished
SENSITIVITY beta scale 2.40 on the final program
SENSITIVITY GRU anchor amplification 1.10
SENSITIVITY GRU anchor amplification 2.00
SENSITIVITY ensemble weight 0.4 linear / 0.6 GRU (0.6/0.4 was tested in 066)
SENSITIVITY state window 3 steps (30min) instead of 6
SENSITIVITY state window 12 steps (2h) instead of 6
SENSITIVITY power-curve resolution 20 bins instead of 40
SENSITIVITY power-curve resolution 80 bins instead of 40
SENSITIVITY meaningful ridge 1e-3 instead of numerical 1e-6
SENSITIVITY sustained-idle window 12h instead of 24h
power curve fitted on generating rows only, so the residual measures underperformance against what a WORKING turbine does rather than against an average that already includes downtime
worst of the three blade pitch angles instead of blade 1 alone (a feathered rotor may show on one blade first)
ambient temperature as an air-density proxy (cold air is denser and carries more power at the same wind speed)
nacelle yaw rate |dNdir| as an activity signal (a turbine actively tracking the wind is under control and running)
cube of wind speed as the available-power proxy (power goes as v^3 below rated); raw wind speed alone was useless in 015
clip predictions to the physical range [0, 1500] kW
farm-wide idle fraction: how much of the SITE is down, which is what a grid curtailment order looks like
two-regime response: turbines idle for more than half the last hour get damped coefficients, since a stopped machine has to restart before it can revert
SENSITIVITY idle threshold 10 kW instead of the physical zero
ABLATION keep only the 24h idle fraction, drop the 1h one
SENSITIVITY persistence ceiling 0.95 instead of full persistence 1.0
CONTROLLED within-class test: GRU member = mean(ckpt_005, seed-1234 ckpt_085); -0.022 and BETTER ON ALL FIVE FOLDS - resolves 012/029, which were confounded by pairing ckpt_005 with a WEAKER partner
seed-1234 GRU alone as the member: 43.133225 against ckpt_005's 43.133271 - equal quality to 5 decimal places, which is what makes 110 interpretable
metric-loss GRU (ckpt_010) as a third member at one sixth weight - the only model that wins on F5
horizon-dependent ensemble weight, GRU heavier over the first day where sequence shape still carries information
climatological anchor from the recent half of training instead of the whole record
per-turbine MEDIAN as the climatological anchor instead of the mean (Patv is heavily right-skewed)
SENSITIVITY residual window 3 steps instead of 6
neighbour idle fraction: whether the turbines around this one are also down, which distinguishes a local outage from a site-wide one
SENSITIVITY beta scale 2.25, between the 2.10 and 2.40 points that tied
stack the two-seed GRU member with a 3-step residual window; -0.011 and better on 4 of 5 folds
two-regime response stacked on the final program: turbines idle more than half the last hour get damped coefficients (106 gave -0.007 standalone)
